purpose: Public-literature and textbook-level strategic disconnection seeds for complex-molecule route critique and proposal-source development.

promotion_requirements: stock or anchor policy separate from strategy match
risk tags for regioselectivity, stereoselectivity, and protecting-group burden

families.name: Macrolides, macrocycles, and polyketide-like polyols
families.strategic_principle: Disconnect macrocycles to linear seco-acid, diene, or amino-acid/peptide-like precursors; disconnect polyketide polyols through stereodefined aldol or crotylation units instead of late product-like protection/deprotection loops.
negative_signals: macrocycle remains intact through only protecting-group changes
no account of high-dilution or oligomerization risk
polyketide stereocenters created without stereochemical strategy

families.name: Indole and monoterpene indole alkaloids
families.strategic_principle: Expose tryptamine/indole nucleophile and aldehyde/iminium partners, especially Pictet-Spengler or strictosidine-like biosynthetic anchors, before elaborating oxidation/rearrangement diversity.

families.name: Benzylisoquinoline and tetrahydroisoquinoline alkaloids
families.strategic_principle: Disconnect the tetrahydroisoquinoline core to a beta-arylethylamine plus carbonyl/iminium precursor, then handle N-methylation, O-methylation, and oxidative phenol coupling as late-stage diversification.

families.name: Glycosides, oligosaccharides, and nucleosides
families.strategic_principle: Disconnect glycosidic bonds to aglycone plus activated/protected sugar donors; for nucleosides, split nucleobase from protected ribose/deoxyribose and track regioselectivity/anomeric selectivity.

families.name: Peptides, depsipeptides, beta-lactams, and antibiotic semisynthesis
families.strategic_principle: Prefer amide/depsipeptide/macrolactam disconnections with protected amino-acid or fermentation-derived beta-lactam cores; do not ask the planner to rebuild complex antibiotic cores when 6-APA/7-ACA-like anchors are the strategic route.

families.name: Taxanes and baccatin semisynthesis
families.strategic_principle: Treat the taxane core as a source-supported advanced natural-product scaffold; disconnect C13 side-chain acylation/carbamate formation and C10 acetylation before considering total synthesis.

families.name: Terpenes and isoprenoid natural products
families.strategic_principle: Use isoprene/prenyl-unit logic, chiral-pool terpene feedstocks, Robinson-annulation scaffolds, or biomimetic cationic/polyene cyclization rather than unstructured ring cleavage.

families.name: Artemisinin and sesquiterpene peroxide scaffolds
families.strategic_principle: Disconnect late peroxide formation to dihydroartemisinic-acid-like sesquiterpene precursors; treat the endoperoxide as a late-stage oxidation/cyclization problem.

families.name: Biaryls, diaryl ethers, and atropisomeric natural products
families.strategic_principle: Expose aryl-aryl or aryl-heteroatom coupling partners and track atropisomerism. For hindered biaryls, coupling order and axial stereocontrol are route-defining, not cosmetic metadata.

families.name: Prostaglandins and eicosanoid-like side-chain architectures
families.strategic_principle: Use a cyclopentane/Corey-lactone-like chiral core and disconnect the two side chains by olefination, organocuprate, or carbonyl homologation logic; preserve alkene geometry and alcohol stereochemistry.

anchors.name: Linear seco-acid / diene macrocycle precursor
anchors.rationale: Macrolactonization, macrolactamization, and RCM are common macrocycle-forming strategies.

break_bonds: macrocyclic ester C-O bond
forward_logic: prepare seco acid with correct stereochemistry
close ring by Yamaguchi, Keck, Mitsunobu, Steglich, or related macrolactonization
use high dilution or conformational control to reduce oligomerization
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward routes that open a macrolactone to a linear precursor with retained stereochemical plan; flag intact-ring protecting-group loops.

evidence.citation: Macrocycle synthesis reviews describe macrolactonization, macrolactamization, RCM, and related approaches as common macrocyclization methods.
Prins-type macrocyclization review summarizes standard macrolactonization conditions such as Yamaguchi, Keck, and Mitsunobu.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: high for linear seco-acid simplification with stereochemistry retained

break_bonds: macrocyclic alkene C=C
forward_logic: prepare terminal or substituted diene precursor
close by RCM or by Julia/HWE alkene-forming macrocyclization
control E/Z geometry and avoid oligomerization
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use RCM as a strategic option when macrolactonization is not the only plausible ring closure.

evidence.citation: Natural products and ring-closing metathesis review.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate when diene precursor substantially simplifies ring closure

disconnections.name: Polyketide polyol to stereodefined aldol fragments

break_bonds: C-C bond adjacent to beta-hydroxy carbonyl or masked aldol unit
forward_logic: use aldol, crotylation, allylation, or ketoreductase logic to set relative stereochemistry
track syn/anti and anti-Felkin/chelation control
delay macrocyclization until linear stereochemistry is established
suggested_precursor_roles: chiral auxiliary or biocatalytic reduction substrate
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Require explicit stereochemical provenance for dense polyketide polyols.

evidence.citation: Macrocycle and polyketide synthesis reviews highlight linear precursor construction before macrocyclization.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: high when aldol fragments reduce complexity and define stereochemistry

break_bonds: C-C bond formed by indole attack on iminium
forward_logic: condense tryptamine or substituted tryptophan derivative with aldehyde/ketone
cyclize by chemical or enzymatic Pictet-Spengler reaction
then elaborate oxidation/rearrangement diversity
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward exposure of tryptamine and aldehyde/iminium partners instead of same-core oxidation/protection variants.

evidence.citation: Strictosidine synthase catalyzes a Pictet-Spengler condensation in monoterpene indole alkaloid biosynthesis.
Sarpagine alkaloid syntheses use asymmetric Pictet-Spengler reactions as key steps.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: high for tryptamine/aldehyde split with stereochemical plan

break_bonds: Pictet-Spengler C-C bond before downstream rearrangements
forward_logic: form strictosidine-like intermediate from tryptamine and secologanin
map downstream rearrangements and oxidations separately
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use as biosynthesis-aware anchor, not as a generic stock solve.

evidence.citation: Strictosidine is a central intermediate in monoterpene indole alkaloid biosynthesis.

break_bonds: C-C bond from aromatic attack on iminium or Bischler cyclodehydration precursor
forward_logic: condense beta-arylethylamine with aldehyde/ketone or amide precursor
cyclize to tetrahydroisoquinoline/dihydroisoquinoline
perform methylation/oxidative coupling downstream
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Expose amine/carbonyl fragments and phenolic oxidative-coupling opportunities.

evidence.citation: Pictet-Spengler reaction forms tetrahydroisoquinoline products from beta-arylethylamine and carbonyl compounds.

break_bonds: anomeric glycosidic bond
forward_logic: prepare protected/activated sugar donor
glycosylate aglycone acceptor chemically or chemoenzymatically
deprotect and adjust anomeric configuration
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Do not leave the whole glycoside core intact; expose sugar/aglycone split and anomeric control.

evidence.citation: Glycosides consist of glycon and aglycon connected through a glycosidic bond formed by glycosylation.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: high when sugar/aglycone split is explicit with anomeric metadata

disconnections.name: Nucleoside base-sugar disconnection

break_bonds: nucleobase N-C anomeric bond
forward_logic: silylate nucleobase and couple with protected electrophilic sugar under Lewis acid conditions
or use enzymatic transglycosylation for base exchange
track N-regioselectivity and anomeric outcome
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Require regioisomer risk tags for purines/pyrimidines and protected sugar compatibility.

risks: C-nucleosides may need C-C bond strategies instead

evidence.citation: Vorbruggen glycosylation is a common route to nucleosides; regioisomers can be a concern.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: high for protected sugar/base split with regioselectivity annotation

disconnections.name: Peptide/depsipeptide amide or ester bond disconnection

target_features: ester linkages between amino/hydroxy acid units
N/C termini or side-chain protecting groups

break_bonds: amide C-N bond
depsipeptide ester C-O bond
macrolactam C-N bond when macrocyclic
forward_logic: disconnect to protected amino acid or hydroxy acid fragments
choose coupling order to minimize epimerization and macrocyclization risk
consider convergent fragment coupling for long peptides
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward chemically conventional peptide fragment splits over arbitrary C-C cleavage.

evidence.citation: Macrocycle synthesis reviews include macrolactamization and peptide-like macrocyclization as common approaches.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: high when amide/ester disconnections map to protected building blocks

disconnections.name: Beta-lactam antibiotic core plus side-chain semisynthesis

break_bonds: side-chain amide C-N bond on beta-lactam nucleus
forward_logic: obtain 6-APA or 7-ACA core from fermentation/semisynthesis
acylate amino nucleus with selected side-chain acid chloride/activated acid
preserve beta-lactam integrity
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Do not reconstruct beta-lactam antibiotic cores from trivial stock when 6-APA/7-ACA is the strategic anchor.

evidence.citation: Semisynthesis of beta-lactam antibiotics from 6-APA and 7-ACA opened major antibiotic families.
Fermentation and organic synthesis are combined industrially for cephalosporins; 7-ACA is a platform core.

break_bonds: C13 ester bond between taxane core and side-chain fragment
C10 acetyl bond if relevant
forward_logic: use baccatin III or 10-deacetylbaccatin III as advanced core
install C13 side chain with Ojima-lactam-like or activated acid side-chain strategy
perform site-selective acylation/deprotection
suggested_precursor_roles: Ojima lactam or side-chain acid equivalent
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Taxane core is a reviewed semisynthesis anchor, not a generic vendor-stock analogue.

evidence.citation: Paclitaxel semisynthesis commonly uses baccatin III or 10-deacetylbaccatin III precursors.
10-deacetylbaccatin III is a key natural product for taxol semisynthesis.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: high when baccatin core and side-chain installation are explicit

break_bonds: peroxide O-O and adjacent oxygenated ring-forming bonds
forward_logic: prepare dihydroartemisinic acid or related unsaturated sesquiterpene acid
form hydroperoxide/endoperoxide by oxygenation/photooxidation/autoxidation sequence
close peroxide-containing ring late
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Classify peroxide construction as a late-stage oxidation/cyclization, not a normal ether disconnection.

evidence.citation: Synthetic peroxide-ring construction reviews highlight dihydroartemisinic acid as a precursor in modern artemisinin production.
Artemisinic acid has been developed as a semisynthesis platform for artemisinin production.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: high when route reaches dihydroartemisinic-acid-like precursor

disconnections.name: Terpene isoprene-unit and cationic cyclization logic

break_bonds: bonds consistent with prenyl-unit assembly or biomimetic cationic cyclization
forward_logic: map carbon skeleton to GPP/FPP/GGPP-like precursor or chiral-pool terpene
use cationic/polyene cyclization, radical cyclization, or Robinson-annulation/chiral pool routes
perform oxidation-state installation after core skeleton is set
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward biogenetic carbon-skeleton mapping; penalize arbitrary ring cleavage that loses stereochemical logic.

evidence.citation: Terpene biosynthesis uses linear isoprene precursors such as GPP, FPP, and GGPP before cyclization.
Terpenoid synthesis reviews discuss total synthesis and origins of terpenoid derivatives.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for prenyl-unit or chiral-pool mapping

disconnections.name: Diels-Alder complexity-generating disconnection

target_classes: alkaloids and terpenoids with DA retrons

break_bonds: two sigma bonds formed in [4+2] cycloaddition
forward_logic: map product ring to diene and dienophile partners
use intramolecular Diels-Alder when tethered precursor simplifies complexity
track endo/exo and regioselectivity
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Generate DA retrons only when electronics and geometry are plausible; label speculative DA routes for review.

risks: biosynthetic DA mimic may not be chemically feasible

evidence.citation: Diels-Alder reactions are widely used in natural product synthesis and biosynthesis-inspired strategies.
Natural Diels-Alderase review connects DA reactions to natural product biosynthesis.

target_features: diaryl ether or phenol oxidative-coupling motif

break_bonds: aryl-aryl bond
aryl-O bond for diaryl ether variants
forward_logic: prepare aryl halide/pseudohalide and aryl boronate/stannane/silane or phenol partners
use Suzuki, Hiyama, Ullmann, oxidative phenol coupling, or enzymatic oxidative coupling
track axial chirality and coupling order
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Do not treat biaryl formation as a generic aryl substitution; atropisomer metadata can be route-defining.

evidence.citation: Hiyama/cross-coupling review notes biaryl scaffolds are common in natural products and pharmaceuticals and can be made by Suzuki, Stille, Negishi, Kumada, Hiyama couplings.
Biocatalytic atropisomer synthesis review covers oxidative coupling approaches to atropisomeric products.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: high when coupling partners and axial stereochemistry are explicit

break_bonds: aryl-aryl or aryl-O bond formed by oxidative coupling
forward_logic: prepare phenolic coupling partners
perform oxidative coupling chemically or enzymatically
control cross-coupling versus homocoupling and atropselectivity
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use when phenolic substitution pattern and biosynthetic precedent support oxidative coupling.

evidence.citation: Biocatalytic atropisomer synthesis examples include P450 oxidative coupling of phenols.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for phenol-pair split with selectivity rationale

target_features: allylic alcohols and E/Z alkene geometry

break_bonds: side-chain C-C bonds attached to cyclopentane core
forward_logic: use Corey-lactone-like chiral cyclopentane intermediate
install alpha and omega side chains by olefination, organocuprate addition, or homologation
track alkene geometry and alcohol stereochemistry
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward convergence to a chiral cyclopentane common intermediate instead of arbitrary lipid-chain fragmentation.

evidence.citation: Corey-style prostaglandin synthesis is a classic strategic use of a chiral cyclopentane/lactone common intermediate.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for Corey-lactone-like core plus side-chain installation

source_notes.summary: Commercial strategic systems such as SYNTHIA/Chematica use large expert-coded rule sets, while open-source systems such as ASKCOS and AiZynthFinder are extensible but mostly template/model driven. This seed file is meant to supply a transparent curated strategic layer.
